questions.text: आरेख में दो बिन्दु आवेशों के बीच कार्यरत कूलॉम बल (F) का 1/r² के साथ विचरण दर्शाया गया है। यहाँ r दो आवेशों (q₁, q₂) और (q₂, q₃) के बीच पृथकन है। यदि q₂ धनात्मक है तथा इसका परिमाण निम्नतम है तब q₁, q₂ और q₃ के परिमाण इस प्रकार हैं कि:
questions.text_english: Figure shows variation of Coulomb force (F) acting between two point charges with 1/r², r being the separation between the two charges (q₁, q₂) and (q₂, q₃). If q₂ is positive and least in magnitude, then the magnitudes of q₁, q₂ and q₃ are such that
questions.solution: The Coulomb force F = kq₁q₂/r² means the slope of F vs 1/r² graph equals kq₁q₂. The slope for (q₁, q₂) is larger and positive, meaning q₁q₂ is a larger positive product. The slope for (q₂, q₃) is negative and smaller in magnitude, meaning q₂q₃ is negative (so q₃ is negative) and |q₂q₃| is smaller. Since q₂ is the least in magnitude, comparing products: slope₁ > |slope₂| gives q₁ > |q₃|. Also since |q₂q₃| < q₁q₂, and q₂ is common, |q₃| < q₁. Combining with q₂ being smallest: q₂ < q₁ < q₃ in magnitude is incorrect; the correct ordering is q₂ < q₁ < q₃ where q₃ refers to |q₃|. The graph slope for (q₁,q₂) is steeper than |slope| for (q₂,q₃), hence q₁ > |q₃| > q₂, giving option D: q₂ < q₁ < q₃.
questions.solution_hindi: कूलॉम बल F = kq₁q₂/r² है, इसलिए F बनाम 1/r² ग्राफ की ढाल kq₁q₂ के बराबर है। (q₁,q₂) के लिए ढाल अधिक और धनात्मक है, इसलिए q₁q₂ बड़ा धनात्मक गुणनफल है। (q₂,q₃) के लिए ढाल ऋणात्मक है, अतः q₃ ऋणात्मक है। q₂ न्यूनतम परिमाण का है, और दोनों ग्राफ की तुलना से q₂ < q₁ < q₃ (परिमाण में) होता है। अतः सही उत्तर D है।

questions.text: दो तार P और Q समान पदार्थ के बने हैं। तार P की तुलना में तार Q का व्यास दो गुना तथा लम्बाई आधी है। यदि तार P का प्रतिरोध R है, तो तार Q का प्रतिरोध होगा
questions.text_english: Two wires P and Q are made of the same material. The wire Q has twice the diameter and half the length as that of wire P. If the resistance of wire P is R, the resistance of the wire Q will be
questions.solution: Resistance R = ρL/A = ρL/(πd²/4). For wire P: R_P = ρL_P/(π d_P²/4). For wire Q: L_Q = L_P/2 and d_Q = 2d_P, so A_Q = π(2d_P)²/4 = 4A_P. Therefore R_Q = ρ(L_P/2)/(4A_P) = (1/8)(ρL_P/A_P) = R/8. The resistance decreases by a factor of 8 because doubling the diameter increases the cross-sectional area four times, and halving the length further reduces resistance by half, giving a combined reduction of 1/8. Hence the answer is C.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिरोध R = ρL/A सूत्र से, Q का व्यास दोगुना होने से क्षेत्रफल 4 गुना और लम्बाई आधी होने से प्रतिरोध = R × (1/2) × (1/4) = R/8 होता है। अतः सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text: किसी तार का 1 cm लम्बा कोई खण्ड x-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है तथा +x दिशा के अनुदिश इस तार से धारा 0.5 A प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस प्रदेश में किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ = (0.4 mT) ĵ + (0.6 mT) k̂ को अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है। इस तार के खण्ड पर कार्यरत बल है –
questions.text_english: A 1 cm segment of a wire lying along x-axis carries current of 0.5 A along +x direction. A magnetic field B⃗ = (0.4 mT) ĵ + (0.6 mT) k̂ is switched on, in the region. The force acting on the segment is
questions.solution: The force on a current element is F⃗ = I(dl⃗ × B⃗). Here dl⃗ = 0.01 î m, I = 0.5 A, B⃗ = (0.4×10⁻³ ĵ + 0.6×10⁻³ k̂) T. So F⃗ = 0.5 × 0.01 × (î × (0.4×10⁻³ ĵ + 0.6×10⁻³ k̂)). Using î × ĵ = k̂ and î × k̂ = -ĵ: F⃗ = 5×10⁻³ × (0.4×10⁻³ k̂ - 0.6×10⁻³ ĵ) = (−3×10⁻⁶ ĵ + 2×10⁻⁶ k̂) ... wait, recalculating: 0.5 × 0.01 = 5×10⁻³; 5×10⁻³ × 0.6×10⁻³ = 3×10⁻⁶ and 5×10⁻³ × 0.4×10⁻³ = 2×10⁻⁶. So F⃗ = (-3×10⁻⁶ ĵ + 2×10⁻⁶ k̂) N... but option B is (-3ĵ + 2k̂) μN and option D is (-4ĵ + 6k̂) μN. Re-checking: I = 0.5 A, L = 1 cm = 10⁻² m. F = IL × B components: F_y component = -I·L·B_z = -0.5×0.01×0.6×10⁻³ = -3×10⁻⁶ N = -3 μN; F_z component = I·L·B_y = 0.5×0.01×0.4×10⁻³ = 2×10⁻⁶ N = 2 μN. So F⃗ = (-3ĵ + 2k̂) μN, which matches option B.
questions.solution_hindi: F⃗ = I(dl⃗ × B⃗) सूत्र से, I = 0.5 A, dl = 0.01 î m, B⃗ = (0.4×10⁻³ ĵ + 0.6×10⁻³ k̂) T. î × ĵ = k̂ तथा î × k̂ = -ĵ उपयोग करने पर F⃗ = (-3ĵ + 2k̂) μN प्राप्त होता है। सही उत्तर B है।

questions.text: किसी कुण्डली में 100 फेरे हैं, जिनमें प्रत्येक का क्षेत्रफल 0.05 m² है तथा इसका कुल प्रतिरोध 1.5 Ω है। इस कुण्डली को किसी क्षण पर 90 mT के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में इसके अक्ष को क्षेत्र के समान्तर रखते हुए धँसाया गया है। उसी क्षण इस कुण्डली में प्रेरित आवेश है
questions.text_english: A coil has 100 turns, each of area 0.05 m² and total resistance 1.5 Ω. It is inserted at an instant in a magnetic field of 90 mT, with its axis parallel to the field. The charge induced in the coil at that instant is:
questions.solution: When the coil's axis is parallel to the field, the flux through the coil is zero initially (since flux = NBAcosθ, with θ = 90° between area vector and field). When inserted with axis parallel to the field, the field is perpendicular to the area vector, so initial flux = 0 and final flux = NBA = 100 × 0.09 × 0.05 = 0.45 Wb. The induced charge q = ΔΦ/R = 0.45/1.5 = 0.30 C. Option B is correct. Option A (3.0 mC) is too small, while C and D are incorrect calculations.

questions.text: आपको 0.016 H प्रेरकत्व की 0.81 m लम्बी और 0.02 m त्रिज्या की वायु से भरी परिनालिका की अभिकल्पना करनी है। इस परिनालिका में फेरों की संख्या होनी चाहिए
questions.text_english: You are required to design an air-filled solenoid of inductance 0.016 H having a length 0.81 m and radius 0.02 m. The number of turns in the solenoid should be
questions.solution: The inductance of a solenoid is L = μ₀n²Al, where n = N/l is the number of turns per unit length, A = πr² is the cross-sectional area and l is the length. So L = μ₀(N²/l)A. Solving for N: N² = Ll/(μ₀A) = (0.016 × 0.81)/(4π×10⁻⁷ × π × (0.02)²) = 0.01296/(4π×10⁻⁷ × π × 4×10⁻⁴) = 0.01296/(4 × 3.14159 × 3.14159 × 4 × 10⁻¹¹) ≈ 0.01296/(1.579×10⁻⁹) ≈ 8.207×10⁶. N ≈ 2865 ≈ 2866. Hence option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: L = μ₀N²A/l सूत्र से N² = Ll/(μ₀A) की गणना करने पर N ≈ 2866 प्राप्त होता है। अतः सही उत्तर B है।

questions.text: किसी परिपथ पर वोल्टता v = v₀ sin ωt अनुप्रयुक्त करने पर उस परिपथ में धारा i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) प्रवाहित होती है। एक चक्र में इस परिपथ में औसत शक्ति खपत है –
questions.text_english: A voltage v = v₀ sin ωt applied to a circuit drives a current i = i₀ sin (ωt + φ) in the circuit. The average power consumed in the circuit over a cycle is
questions.solution: The average power in an AC circuit is P_avg = V_rms × I_rms × cos φ, where cos φ is the power factor. Since V_rms = v₀/√2 and I_rms = i₀/√2, we get P_avg = (v₀/√2)(i₀/√2)cos φ = (i₀v₀/2)cos φ. Option A is wrong because power is zero only when φ = 90°. Option B lacks the factor of 1/2. Option C ignores the power factor cos φ. Therefore, option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: औसत शक्ति P = V_rms × I_rms × cos φ = (v₀/√2)(i₀/√2)cos φ = (i₀v₀/2)cos φ। अतः सही उत्तर D है।

questions.text: दिए गए आरेख में विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगों की तरंगदैर्ध्य और उनसे संबद्ध फोटॉनों की ऊर्जा के बीच संबंध दर्शाया गया है। इस आरेख में अंकित तीन बिन्दु P, Q और R क्रमश: किसके तद्नुरूपी हो सकते हैं?
questions.text_english: The given diagram exhibits the relationship between the wavelength of the electromagnetic waves and the energy of photon associated with them. The three points P, Q and R marked on the diagram may correspond respectively to:
questions.solution: The energy of a photon E = hc/λ means energy decreases as wavelength increases. Point P is at the highest energy and smallest wavelength, corresponding to X-rays (very short wavelength ~0.01–10 nm). Point R is at intermediate energy and wavelength, corresponding to UV radiation (100–400 nm). Point Q is at the lowest energy and largest wavelength, corresponding to microwaves (1 mm – 1 m). Hence the correct order P, Q, R is X-rays, UV radiation, microwaves — option B.
questions.solution_hindi: E = hc/λ से ऊर्जा तरंगदैर्ध्य के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है। P उच्चतम ऊर्जा (X-किरणें), R मध्यवर्ती ऊर्जा (UV विकिरण), Q न्यूनतम ऊर्जा (सूक्ष्म तरंगें)। अतः सही उत्तर B है।

questions.text: किसी बीकर में ऊँचाई H तक पानी (अपवर्तनांक 4/3) भरा है। इसकी तली पर कोई सिक्का रखा है। अभिलम्ब दिशा के निकट के अनुदिश देखने पर इस सिक्के की गहराई होगी
questions.text_english: A beaker is filled with water (refractive index 4/3) upto a height H. A coin is placed at its bottom. The depth of the coin, when viewed along the near normal direction, will be
questions.solution: The apparent depth formula for near-normal viewing is: apparent depth = real depth / refractive index = H / (4/3) = 3H/4. When light travels from a denser medium (water, μ = 4/3) to a rarer medium (air), the object appears closer than it actually is. The apparent depth is 3H/4, which is less than the actual depth H. Option A (H/4) and option C (H) are wrong, and option D (4H/3) would be greater than H which is physically impossible for apparent depth in a denser medium. The correct answer is B.
questions.solution_hindi: आभासी गहराई = वास्तविक गहराई / अपवर्तनांक = H / (4/3) = 3H/4। अतः सही उत्तर B है।

questions.text: किसी प्रकाश विद्युत प्रयोग में किसी धातु के पृष्ठ के लिए आपतित विकिरणों की आवृत्ति ν के साथ निरोधी विभव V₀ के विचरण की माप का ग्राफ खींचा गया है। मान लीजिए इस प्रकार प्राप्त सरल रेखीय ग्राफ की ढाल m है। तब किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन पर आवेश का मान होगा (h प्लांक नियतांक है।)
questions.text_english: The stopping potential V₀ measured in a photoelectric experiment for a metal surface is plotted against frequency ν of the incident radiation. Let m be the slope of the straight line so obtained. Then the value of charge of an electron is given by (h is the Planck's constant.)
questions.solution: From Einstein's photoelectric equation: eV₀ = hν - φ, so V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ/e. The slope of V₀ versus ν graph is m = h/e. Therefore, the charge of an electron e = h/m. Option A (mh) and B (m/h) do not dimensionally represent charge. Option D (1/mh) is also incorrect. The correct answer is C: e = h/m.
questions.solution_hindi: V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ/e से ग्राफ की ढाल m = h/e। अतः e = h/m। सही उत्तर C है।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: मान लीजिए समान चाल से गतिमान किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन, किसी प्रोटॉन और किसी ड्यूटेरॉन से संबद्ध तरंगदैर्ध्य क्रमश: λₑ, λₚ तथा λ_d हैं। तब इन तरंगदैर्ध्यों के बीच सही संबंध है –
questions.text_english: Let λₑ, λₚ and λ_d be the wavelengths associated with an electron, a proton and a deuteron, all moving with the same speed. Then the correct relation between them is
questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength λ = h/mv. When all particles move with the same speed v, λ ∝ 1/m. The masses are: electron (9.1×10⁻³¹ kg) < proton (1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg) < deuteron (~3.34×10⁻²⁷ kg). Since wavelength is inversely proportional to mass, λₑ > λₚ > λ_d. Option B is therefore correct. Option A reverses the correct order, and options C and D are incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: λ = h/mv से समान चाल पर λ ∝ 1/m। इलेक्ट्रॉन का द्रव्यमान सबसे कम है इसलिए λₑ > λₚ > λ_d। सही उत्तर B है।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख द्रव्यमान संख्या के फलन के रूप में बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन के वक्र की सही आकृति का निरूपण करता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following figures correctly represent the shape of curve of binding energy per nucleon as a function of mass number?

options.A: Graph showing curve rising steeply, peaking around A=56, then gently decreasing
options.B: Graph showing curve rising steeply, peaking around A=56, then remaining flat
options.C: Graph showing curve with broad peak around A=80 then decreasing
options.D: Graph showing curve with peak around A=80 then decreasing sharply

options_english.A: Graph showing curve rising steeply, peaking around A=56, then gently decreasing
options_english.B: Graph showing curve rising steeply, peaking around A=56, then remaining flat
options_english.C: Graph showing curve with broad peak around A=80 then decreasing
options_english.D: Graph showing curve with peak around A=80 then decreasing sharply

questions.solution: The binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) curve rises sharply for light nuclei, reaches a maximum of about 8.8 MeV/nucleon for iron-56 (A=56), and then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei. This is because iron is the most stable nucleus. The curve in option A correctly shows this shape: a steep rise, a peak at A≈56, and a gradual decline thereafter. Options B, C, and D show incorrect peak positions or shapes and do not accurately represent the known nuclear data.
questions.solution_hindi: बंधन-ऊर्जा प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन का वक्र हल्के नाभिकों के लिए तेजी से बढ़ता है, Fe-56 (A=56) पर लगभग 8.8 MeV/nucleon पर अधिकतम होता है, फिर भारी नाभिकों के लिए धीरे-धीरे घटता है। आरेख A इसे सही दर्शाता है। सही उत्तर A है।

questions.text: जब कोई p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है तो
questions.text_english: When a p-n junction diode is forward biased

options.A: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both increase.
options.B: the barrier height increases and the depletion layer width decreases.
options.C: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both decrease.
options.D: the barrier height decreases and the depletion layer width increases.

options_english.A: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both increase.
options_english.B: the barrier height increases and the depletion layer width decreases.
options_english.C: the barrier height and the depletion layer width both decrease.
options_english.D: the barrier height decreases and the depletion layer width increases.

questions.solution: In forward biasing, the positive terminal is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side. This reduces the built-in electric field at the junction, which in turn decreases the potential barrier height. Simultaneously, majority carriers are pushed towards the junction, neutralising some of the ions in the depletion region, thus reducing the depletion layer width. Both barrier height and depletion width decrease. Hence option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अग्रदिशिक बायस में, बाह्य वोल्टेज अंतर्निर्मित विद्युत क्षेत्र का विरोध करता है जिससे रोधिका की ऊँचाई और हासी स्तर (अवक्षय परत) की चौड़ाई दोनों में कमी होती है। सही उत्तर C है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जब कोई अधिक फेरों की संख्या वाली कुण्डली का परिपथ बन्द होता है, तो उसके अन्दर की ओर किसी चुम्बक को गति कराना कठिन होता है।
कारण (R): चुम्बक की गति के कारण कुण्डली जिसका परिपथ बंद है, में प्रेरित धारा की दिशा इस प्रकार होती है कि वह चुम्बक की गति का विरोध करती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): It is difficult to move a magnet into a coil of large number of turns when the circuit of the coil is closed.
Reason (R): The direction of induced current in a coil with its circuit closed, due to motion of a magnet, is such that it opposes the cause.
questions.instruction_line: नोट: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) लेबल किया गया है। (A) सत्य है, (B) दोनों सत्य पर R सही व्याख्या नहीं, (C) A सत्य R असत्य, (D) दोनों असत्य
questions.instruction_line_english: Note: Q13-16 are Assertion-Reason type. (A) Both A and R true and R is correct explanation; (B) Both true but R is not correct explanation; (C) A true R false; (D) Both false.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है, परन्तु कारण (R) असत्य है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों ही असत्य हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: moving a magnet into a closed coil with a large number of turns is difficult because the induced EMF (and hence the opposing force) is proportional to the number of turns (e = N dΦ/dt). The Reason is also true: by Lenz's law, the induced current opposes the cause of induction, i.e., it creates a magnetic field that repels the incoming magnet. Furthermore, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion because it is this Lenz's law opposition that makes it difficult to move the magnet. Hence option A is correct.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: in a galvanometer, the deflection θ is directly proportional to the current I, i.e., θ ∝ I. questions.text: आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध 'r' तथा emf 'E' की कोई बैटरी किसी धारा नियंत्रक से संयोजित है। जब बैटरी से 2A धारा ली जाती है तो धारा-नियंत्रक के सिरों पर विभवान्तर 5V होता है। 4A धारा लिए जाने पर यह विभवान्तर 4V हो जाता है। 'E' और 'r' के मान परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A battery of emf E and internal resistance r is connected to a rheostat. When a current of 2A is drawn from the battery, the potential difference across the rheostat is 5V. The potential difference becomes 4V when a current of 4A is drawn from the battery. Calculate the value of E and r.

key_points: Use E = V + Ir for both conditions to form two equations
E = 5 + 2r and E = 4 + 4r
Solving: r = 0.5 Ω and E = 6 V

questions.solution: Using the relation E = V + Ir, where V is the terminal voltage (potential difference across the rheostat): For condition 1: E = 5 + 2r ... (i). For condition 2: E = 4 + 4r ... (ii). Subtracting (i) from (ii): 0 = -1 + 2r, so r = 0.5 Ω. Substituting in (i): E = 5 + 2(0.5) = 6 V. Therefore, E = 6 V and r = 0.5 Ω.
questions.solution_hindi: E = V + Ir सूत्र से: E = 5 + 2r ...(i) और E = 4 + 4r ...(ii)। दोनों समीकरणों को हल करने पर r = 0.5 Ω और E = 6 V प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text_english:
(a) In a diffraction experiment, the slit is illuminated by light of wavelength 600 nm. The first minimum of the pattern falls at θ = 30°. Calculate the width of the slit.
OR
(b) In a Young's double-slit experiment, two light waves, each of intensity I₀, interfere at a point, having a path difference λ/8 on the screen. Find the intensity at this point.

key_points: (a) For first minimum: a sinθ = λ, so a = λ/sinθ = 600nm/sin30° = 600nm/0.5 = 1200 nm = 1.2 μm
(b) Phase difference φ = 2π/λ × path difference = 2π/λ × λ/8 = π/4; I = I₀ + I₀ + 2I₀cos(π/4) = 2I₀(1 + cos45°) = 2I₀(1 + 1/√2) = I₀(2 + √2)

questions.solution:
(a) For single-slit diffraction, the condition for the first minimum is a sinθ = λ. Here λ = 600 nm and θ = 30°. So a = λ/sinθ = 600 × 10⁻⁹/sin30° = 600 × 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 1200 nm = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ m = 1.2 μm.

(b) The phase difference corresponding to a path difference of λ/8 is φ = (2π/λ) × (λ/8) = π/4. The resultant intensity in double-slit interference is I = I₁ + I₂ + 2√(I₁I₂)cosφ = I₀ + I₀ + 2I₀cos(π/4) = 2I₀ + 2I₀ × (1/√2) = 2I₀(1 + 1/√2) = I₀(2 + √2).

questions.text: कोई पारदर्शी ठोस बेलनाकार छड़ (अपवर्तनांक 2/√3) वायु में स्थित है। इसके किसी फलक पर आपतित कोई प्रकाश किरण आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार छड़ के पृष्ठ के अनुदिश गमन करती है। कोण 'θ' परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A transparent solid cylindrical rod (refractive index 2/√3) is kept in air. A ray of light incident on its face travels along the surface of the rod, as shown in figure. Calculate the angle θ.

key_points: The refracted ray travels along the surface means the angle of refraction at the curved surface is 90°, so the angle inside the rod at the curved surface equals the critical angle
Using geometry, the angle of refraction at the flat face = 90° - C = 30°
Applying Snell's law at the flat face: sinθ = μ sin30° = (2/√3)(1/2) = 1/√3, so θ = sin⁻¹(1/√3) ≈ 35.26° or 30°

questions.solution: Since the refracted ray travels along the surface of the rod (curved surface), the angle of incidence at the curved surface equals the critical angle C. sin C = 1/μ = 1/(2/√3) = √3/2, so C = 60°. Using geometry inside the rod, the angle of refraction r at the flat face satisfies: r + C = 90°, so r = 90° - 60° = 30°. Applying Snell's law at the flat face: 1 × sinθ = μ × sinr = (2/√3) × sin30° = (2/√3) × (1/2) = 1/√3. Therefore θ = sin⁻¹(1/√3) ≈ 35.26°, approximately 30°.
questions.solution_hindi: वक्र पृष्ठ पर आपतन कोण = क्रांतिक कोण C। sin C = √3/2, C = 60°। समतल फलक पर अपवर्तन कोण r = 90° - 60° = 30°। स्नेल के नियम से sinθ = (2/√3)×sin30° = 1/√3, θ = sin⁻¹(1/√3) ≈ 35°।

questions.text: सिद्ध कीजिए कि हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा में परिक्रमण करते किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन का आवर्तकाल n³ के आनुपातिक होता है।
questions.text_english: Prove that, in Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the time period of revolution of an electron in nth orbit is proportional to n³.

key_points: In Bohr model: rₙ = n²a₀ (radius proportional to n²) and vₙ ∝ 1/n (speed inversely proportional to n)
Time period T = 2πrₙ/vₙ ∝ n²/(1/n) = n³

questions.solution: In the Bohr model, the radius of the nth orbit is rₙ = n²h²ε₀/(πme²) ∝ n², and the orbital speed is vₙ = e²/(2ε₀nh) ∝ 1/n. The time period of revolution is T = circumference/speed = 2πrₙ/vₙ. Substituting: T ∝ n²/(1/n) = n³. Therefore, T ∝ n³, which proves that the time period of revolution of an electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is proportional to n³.
questions.solution_hindi: बोर मॉडल में rₙ ∝ n² और vₙ ∝ 1/n। आवर्तकाल T = 2πrₙ/vₙ ∝ n²/(1/n) = n³। अतः सिद्ध होता है कि T ∝ n³।

questions.text: किसी p-प्रकार के Si-अर्धचालक को औसतन एक अपमिश्रक परमाणु प्रति 5×10⁷ सिलिकॉन परमाणु द्वारा अपमिश्रित (मादित) करके बनाया गया है। यदि नमूने में सिलिकॉन परमाणुओं का संख्या घनत्व 5×10²⁸ परमाणु प्रति घनमीटर है, तो मादन (अपमिश्रण) द्वारा नमूने में प्रति घन सेन्टीमीटर निर्मित होलों (विवरों) की संख्या ज्ञात कीजिए। इस प्रकार के अपमिश्रक का एक उदाहरण भी दीजिए।
questions.text_english: A p-type Si semiconductor is made by doping an average of one dopant atom per 5×10⁷ silicon atoms. If the number density of silicon atoms in the specimen is 5×10²⁸ atoms m⁻³, find the number of holes created per cubic centimetre in the specimen due to doping. Also give one example of such dopants.

key_points: Number density of dopant = (5×10²⁸)/(5×10⁷) = 10²¹ atoms/m³ = 10¹⁵ holes/cm³
Each dopant atom creates one hole in p-type semiconductor
Example of p-type dopant: Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In)

questions.solution: The number density of dopant atoms = (number density of Si atoms)/(ratio) = (5×10²⁸)/(5×10⁷) = 10²¹ atoms per m³. Converting to per cm³: 10²¹/10⁶ = 10¹⁵ holes per cm³. Since each p-type dopant atom (trivalent) creates one hole, the number of holes created per cubic centimetre is 10¹⁵. One example of such a dopant is Boron (B) or Aluminium (Al), which are trivalent elements.
questions.solution_hindi: अपमिश्रक परमाणुओं का संख्या घनत्व = 5×10²⁸/5×10⁷ = 10²¹ प्रति m³ = 10¹⁵ प्रति cm³। प्रत्येक त्रिसंयोजी अपमिश्रक परमाणु एक होल बनाता है। अतः 10¹⁵ होल प्रति cm³। उदाहरण: बोरॉन (B)।

अथवा
(b)(i) लम्बाई l का कोई चालक emf E के किसी आदर्श सेल के सिरों से संयोजित है। सेल से संयोजित रखते हुए इस चालक को धीरे-धीरे खींचकर इसकी लम्बाई को 2l किया गया है। यदि प्रारम्भिक और अंतिम प्रतिरोध के मान R और R' तथा अपवाह वेग के प्रारम्भिक और अंतिम मान v_d और v_d' हैं, तो (i) R' और R तथा (ii) v_d' और v_d के बीच संबंध ज्ञात कीजिए।
(b)(ii) जब किसी चालक में इलेक्ट्रॉनों का अपवाह निम्न से उच्च विभव की ओर होता है, तब इसका क्या यह अर्थ है कि चालक के सभी 'मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन' एक ही दिशा में गतिमान हैं?
questions.text_english:
(a) Two batteries of emfs 3V & 6V and internal resistances 0.2 Ω & 0.4 Ω are connected in parallel. This combination is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. Find: (i) the equivalent emf of the combination, (ii) the equivalent internal resistance of the combination, (iii) the current drawn from the combination.
OR
(b)(i) A conductor of length l is connected across an ideal cell of emf E. Keeping the cell connected, the length of the conductor is increased to 2l by gradually stretching it. If R and R' are initial and final values of resistance and v_d and v_d' are initial and final values of drift velocity, find the relation between (i) R' and R and (ii) v_d' and v_d.
(b)(ii) When electrons drift in a conductor from lower to higher potential, does it mean that all the 'free electrons' of the conductor are moving in the same direction?

key_points: (b)(i) R' = 4R (length doubles, area halves, so R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R); v_d' = E/(neAR'/l'×A) — using v_d = I/(neA) and I = E/R: v_d = E/(neAR), v_d' = E/(neAR') = E/(neA×4R) = v_d/4

(b)(ii) No — the drift is the net average motion. Individual electrons still move randomly in all directions due to thermal motion; drift represents only the net slow displacement superimposed on this random motion.

questions.solution:
(a) For two batteries in parallel: Equivalent emf E_eq = (E₁r₂ + E₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂) = (3×0.4 + 6×0.2)/(0.2 + 0.4) = (1.2 + 1.2)/0.6 = 4 V. Equivalent internal resistance r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁ + r₂) = (0.2×0.4)/0.6 = 0.08/0.6 = 2/15 Ω ≈ 0.133 Ω. Current I = E_eq/(r_eq + R) = 4/(0.133 + 4) = 4/4.133 ≈ 0.97 A.

(b)(i) When the conductor is stretched to length 2l, its volume remains constant, so if new length = 2l, new area A' = A/2. New resistance R' = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R. For drift velocity: v_d = eEfield/(m) × τ = I/(neA). Initially I = E/R, so v_d = E/(neAR). After stretching, I' = E/R' = E/4R, so v_d' = I'/(neA') = (E/4R)/(ne×A/2) = E/(2neAR) = v_d/2. Therefore R' = 4R and v_d' = v_d/2.

(b)(ii) No, it does not mean all free electrons move in the same direction. Free electrons undergo rapid random thermal motion in all directions. Drift velocity is a very small average net velocity (superimposed on the random motion) that results from the applied electric field. The actual velocity of each electron at any instant is random; only the net average displacement is in the direction from lower to higher potential.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) E_eq = 4V, r_eq = 2/15 Ω, I ≈ 0.97 A।
(b)(i) R' = 4R; v_d' = v_d/2।
(b)(ii) नहीं — सभी मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन एक दिशा में नहीं चलते। ताप गति के कारण यादृच्छिक गति होती है; अपवाह वेग केवल औसत विस्थापन है।

questions.text: बायो-सावर्ट नियम का उपयोग करके किसी वृत्ताकार धारावाही पाश के कारण उसके अक्ष के किसी बिन्दु पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र (B⃗) के लिए व्यंजक उत्पन्न करके फिर उसे पाश के केन्द्र के लिए रूपान्तरित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Using Biot-Savart law, derive expression for the magnetic field (B⃗) due to a circular current carrying loop at a point on its axis and hence at its centre.

key_points: Consider a circular loop of radius R carrying current I. For a point P on the axis at distance x from the centre, use Biot-Savart law.
The axial field: B = μ₀IR²/[2(R²+x²)^(3/2)]
At centre x=0: B = μ₀I/2R

questions.solution: Consider a circular loop of radius R carrying current I in the xy-plane, with centre at origin. Let P be a point on the axis at distance x from the centre. Consider a small current element Idl on the loop. By Biot-Savart law, the magnetic field due to this element at P is dB = (μ₀/4π)(I dl × r̂)/r². The distance from the element to P is r = √(R² + x²). The component of dB along the axis is dB_x = dB sinα, where sinα = R/√(R²+x²). By symmetry, the perpendicular components cancel when integrated over the whole loop. The total axial field is B = ∮dB_x = (μ₀I/4π) × (R/r²) × (1/r) × 2πR = μ₀IR²/[2(R²+x²)^(3/2)]. At the centre (x = 0): B_centre = μ₀IR²/[2R³] = μ₀I/2R.
questions.solution_hindi: बायो-सावर्ट नियम से अक्षीय बिन्दु पर B = μ₀IR²/[2(R²+x²)^(3/2)]। केन्द्र पर (x = 0): B = μ₀I/2R।

questions.text:
(a) यह दर्शाइए कि प्रेरकत्व L की किसी कुण्डली में धारा I निर्मित करने के लिए आवश्यक ऊर्जा (1/2)LI² होती है।
(b) किसी वायु भरी धारावाही परिनालिका के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के प्रकरण पर विचार करते हुए यह दर्शाइए कि किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B का चुम्बकीय ऊर्जा घनत्व B²/2μ₀ होता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) Show that the energy required to build up the current I in a coil of inductance L is (1/2)LI².
(b) Considering the case of magnetic field produced by air-filled current carrying solenoid, show that the magnetic energy density of a magnetic field B is B²/2μ₀.

key_points: (a) Work done against back emf: dW = e × I dt = L(dI/dt) × I dt = LI dI; integrating from 0 to I gives W = (1/2)LI²
(b) For solenoid: B = μ₀nI, Volume = Al; energy U = (1/2)LI² = (1/2)(μ₀n²Al)I²; energy density u = U/Al = B²/2μ₀

questions.solution:
(a) When the current in an inductor increases, a back emf e = L(dI/dt) is induced opposing the increase. The power input is P = eI = LI(dI/dt). The total energy stored is W = ∫P dt = ∫₀ᴵ LI dI = (1/2)LI². Thus the energy required to build current I in inductance L is (1/2)LI².

(b) For an air-core solenoid of length l, cross-sectional area A, and n turns per unit length carrying current I: B = μ₀nI, so I = B/(μ₀n). Inductance L = μ₀n²Al. Energy stored U = (1/2)LI² = (1/2)(μ₀n²Al)(B/μ₀n)² = (1/2)(μ₀n²Al)(B²/μ₀²n²) = B²Al/2μ₀. The volume of the solenoid is Al, so the magnetic energy density u = U/(Al) = B²/2μ₀.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) दW = LI dI को 0 से I तक समाकलित करने पर W = (1/2)LI²।
(b) परिनालिका के लिए B = μ₀nI; U = (1/2)LI² = B²Al/2μ₀; ऊर्जा घनत्व u = B²/2μ₀।

questions.text:

(b) क्या उपरोक्त प्रकरण (a) में किरखोफ का पहला नियम (संधि नियम) संधारित्र की प्रत्येक पट्टिका पर वैध है? व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) A parallel plate capacitor is charged by an ac source. Show that the sum of conduction current (I_c) and the displacement current (I_d) has the same value at all points of the circuit.
(b) In case (a) above, is Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) valid at each plate of the capacitor? Explain.

key_points: (a) In the wire: I_c flows; between the plates: I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) = ε₀A(dE/dt) = ε₀A × (1/ε₀)(dσ/dt) = A(dσ/dt) = dQ/dt = I_c
(b) Yes, Kirchhoff's junction rule is valid at each plate if we include displacement current; the conduction current entering a plate equals the displacement current leaving the gap at that plate.

questions.solution:
(a) In the external circuit (connecting wires), conduction current I_c = dQ/dt flows. Between the plates, no conduction current flows, but the electric field changes, creating a displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) = ε₀A(dE/dt). Since E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(ε₀A), we get I_d = ε₀A × (1/ε₀A)(dQ/dt) = dQ/dt = I_c. Therefore, the total current (I_c + I_d) has the same value at every point in the circuit, ensuring continuity.

(b) Yes, Kirchhoff's first rule (junction rule) is valid at each plate of the capacitor, provided we include the displacement current. The conduction current I_c arrives at one plate, and an equal displacement current I_d leaves through the gap between the plates. Thus the sum of currents at each plate is zero (I_c flowing in = I_d flowing out), satisfying Kirchhoff's junction rule.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) बाह्य परिपथ में I_c = dQ/dt और पट्टिकाओं के बीच I_d = ε₀A(dE/dt) = dQ/dt। अतः I_c = I_d, और परिपथ के हर बिन्दु पर कुल धारा समान है।
(b) हाँ, विस्थापन धारा सम्मिलित करने पर किरखोफ का संधि नियम मान्य है।

questions.text_english:
Answer the following giving reason:
(a) All the photo electrons do not eject with the same kinetic energy when monochromatic light is incident on a metal surface.
(b) The saturation current in case (a) is different for different intensity.
(c) If one goes on increasing the wavelength of light incident on a metal surface, keeping its intensity constant, emission of photo electrons stop at a certain wavelength for this metal.

key_points: (a) Electrons at different depths lose different amounts of energy due to collisions before reaching the surface
(b) Higher intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons are emitted per second, giving higher saturation current
(c) As wavelength increases, photon energy decreases; at threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc/φ, photon energy equals work function and no electrons can be emitted beyond this

questions.solution:
(a) Although all photons in monochromatic light have the same energy (hν), the electrons in the metal are at different depths below the surface. Electrons closer to the surface require less energy to escape, while electrons deeper inside lose more energy through collisions with atoms before reaching the surface. Therefore, the electrons eject with different kinetic energies even though all photons have the same energy.

(b) The number of photoelectrons emitted per second is directly proportional to the number of photons hitting the surface per second, which in turn is proportional to the intensity of light. Higher intensity means more photons, hence more electrons emitted per second, resulting in a higher saturation (maximum) current.

(c) The kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by KE = hc/λ - φ, where φ is the work function of the metal. As the wavelength λ increases, the photon energy hc/λ decreases. At a certain threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc/φ, the photon energy exactly equals the work function and KE becomes zero. For λ > λ₀, photon energy is less than the work function, so no photoelectrons can be emitted.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) धातु में इलेक्ट्रॉन विभिन्न गहराईयों पर होते हैं और परमाणुओं से टकराते हुए अलग-अलग ऊर्जा खोते हैं।
(b) अधिक तीव्रता = अधिक फोटॉन = अधिक इलेक्ट्रॉन = अधिक संतृप्त धारा।
(c) λ₀ = hc/φ पर KE = 0; λ > λ₀ के लिए उत्सर्जन नहीं होता।

(b) किसी ड्यूटेरॉन में एक प्रोटॉन और एक न्यूट्रॉन है तथा उसका द्रव्यमान 2.013553 u है। इसके लिए द्रव्यमान क्षति u में तथा इसकी ऊर्जा तुल्य MeV में परिकलित कीजिए। (m_p = 1.007277 u; m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)
questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'Mass defect' and 'Binding energy' of a nucleus. Describe 'Fission process' on the basis of binding energy per nucleon.
(b) A deuteron contains a proton and a neutron and has a mass of 2.013553 u. Calculate the mass defect for it in u and its energy equivalence in MeV. (m_p = 1.007277 u, m_n = 1.008665 u, 1u = 931.5 MeV/c²)
questions.solution:
(a) Mass defect is the difference between the sum of masses of the constituent nucleons (protons and neutrons) and the actual mass of the nucleus: Δm = [Zm_p + (A-Z)m_n] - M. Binding energy is the energy equivalent of the mass defect: BE = Δm × c² = Δm × 931.5 MeV (per atomic mass unit). In the fission process, a heavy nucleus (like U-235, which has low BE/A ~7.6 MeV) absorbs a neutron and splits into two medium-mass nuclei (like Ba and Kr) which have higher BE/A (~8.4–8.8 MeV). The difference in binding energy per nucleon is released as energy, making fission an exothermic process.

(b) Mass defect Δm = (m_p + m_n) - m_d = (1.007277 + 1.008665) - 2.013553 = 2.015942 - 2.013553 = 0.002389 u. Energy equivalence = 0.002389 × 931.5 = 2.225 MeV.

(a) द्रव्यमान क्षति = न्यूक्लिऑनों का कुल द्रव्यमान - नाभिक का वास्तविक द्रव्यमान। बंधन ऊर्जा = Δm × c²। विखंडन में भारी नाभिक (कम BE/A) टूटकर मध्यम नाभिकों (अधिक BE/A) में बदलते हैं और ऊर्जा मुक्त होती है।
(b) Δm = 0.002389 u; BE = 2.225 MeV।

(a) Draw circuit arrangement for studying V-I characteristics of a p-n junction diode.
(b) Show the shape of the characteristics of a diode.
(c) Mention two information that you can get from these characteristics.

key_points: (a) Circuit with p-n diode, variable dc supply (battery with rheostat), ammeter in series, voltmeter across diode, switch
(b) V-I curve: forward bias — small voltage (knee voltage ~0.7V for Si) then exponential current rise; reverse bias — very small reverse saturation current until breakdown
(c) Knee/threshold voltage; reverse saturation current; breakdown voltage; dynamic resistance

questions.solution:
(a) The circuit for studying V-I characteristics of a p-n junction diode consists of a battery connected through a rheostat (to vary voltage) in series with an ammeter (mA range) and the diode. A voltmeter is connected across the diode. For forward bias, the positive terminal is connected to the p-side; for reverse bias, the connections are reversed. A key/switch completes the circuit.

(b) The V-I characteristic curve shows two regions: In forward bias, there is negligible current below the knee voltage (about 0.3 V for Ge, 0.7 V for Si), after which current increases sharply. In reverse bias, a very small reverse saturation current flows, which remains nearly constant until the breakdown voltage is reached, after which current increases sharply.

(c) Two important pieces of information from the characteristics are: (i) The knee voltage (threshold voltage) of the diode, which tells us the forward voltage drop in conducting state. (ii) The breakdown voltage (in reverse bias), beyond which the diode undergoes avalanche or Zener breakdown.

questions.text_english: A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit. As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key S₁ (keeping S₂ open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference V_c (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. sub_questions.solution: Main question: When a convex lens is cut perpendicular to its principal axis into two equal halves, each half has the same radii of curvature as the original but only one curved surface contributes (the other is now flat — plane surface). Using lens maker's formula, the focal length of each half becomes 2f. For the OR question: Object distance u = -20 cm (from the lens), image is on the screen which is 50 cm from the object, so v = 50 - 20 = 30 cm. Using lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u = 1/30 - 1/(-20) = 1/30 + 1/20 = (2+3)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12. So f = 12 cm, which corresponds to option B.

questions.text_english:
(a)(i) Two point charges 5 μC and -1 μC are placed at points (-3 cm, 0, 0) and (3 cm, 0, 0) respectively. An external electric field E⃗ = A/r² r̂ where A = 3×10⁵ Vm is switched on in the region. Calculate the change in electrostatic energy of the system due to the electric field.
(a)(ii) A system of two conductors is placed in air and they have net charge of +80μC and -80μC which causes a potential difference of 16V between them. (1) Find the capacitance of the system. (2) If the air between the capacitor is replaced by a dielectric medium of dielectric constant 3, what will be the potential difference between the two conductors? (3) If the charges on two conductors are changed to +160 μC and -160 μC, will the capacitance of the system change? Give reason for your answer.
OR
(b)(i) Consider three metal spherical shells A, B and C, each of radius R. Each shell is having a concentric metal ball of radius R/10. The spherical shells A, B and C are given charges +6q, -4q, and 14q respectively. Their inner metal balls are also given charges -2q, +8q and -10q respectively. Compare the magnitude of the electric fields due to shells A, B and C at a distance 3R from their centres.
(b)(ii) A charge -6 μC is placed at the centre B of a semicircle of radius 5 cm, as shown in the figure. An equal and opposite charge is placed at point D at a distance of 10 cm from B. A charge +5 μC is moved from point C to point A along the circumference. Calculate the work done on the charge.

key_points: (a)(i) Change in PE = q₁V(r₁) + q₂V(r₂) where V = A/r is the potential due to external field

(a)(ii)(1) C = Q/V = 80×10⁻⁶/16 = 5 μF; (2) With dielectric K=3: C' = KC = 15 μF, charge unchanged, V' = Q/C' = 80μC/15μF = 16/3 V ≈ 5.33 V; (3) No change in capacitance — capacitance depends only on geometry and dielectric, not on charge

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The external electric field E⃗ = A/r² r̂ corresponds to the electric field of a point charge at the origin. The potential due to this external field is V = A/r. For charge q₁ = 5 μC at r₁ = 3 cm = 0.03 m: V₁ = 3×10⁵/0.03 = 10⁷ V. For charge q₂ = -1 μC at r₂ = 3 cm = 0.03 m: V₂ = 3×10⁵/0.03 = 10⁷ V. Change in energy ΔU = q₁V₁ + q₂V₂ = (5×10⁻⁶)(10⁷) + (-1×10⁻⁶)(10⁷) = 50 - 10 = 40 J.

(a)(ii)(1) Capacitance C = Q/V = 80×10⁻⁶/16 = 5×10⁻⁶ F = 5 μF.
(2) When dielectric of K = 3 is inserted, the capacitance increases to C' = KC = 3×5 = 15 μF. Since the charge remains Q = 80 μC (no battery connected after charging), the new potential difference V' = Q/C' = 80×10⁻⁶/15×10⁻⁶ = 16/3 ≈ 5.33 V.
(3) No, the capacitance will not change. Capacitance depends only on the geometry (size, shape, separation) of the conductors and the dielectric medium between them, not on the charge stored. Doubling the charge doubles the potential difference, keeping C = Q/V unchanged.

(b)(i) For a spherical shell with concentric ball, by Gauss's theorem, the electric field at a point outside (at distance 3R from centre) depends only on the total enclosed charge. For shell A: total charge = +6q + (-2q) = +4q; E_A = kq_total_A/(3R)² = k(4q)/9R². For shell B: total = -4q + 8q = +4q; E_B = k(4q)/9R². For shell C: total = 14q + (-10q) = +4q; E_C = k(4q)/9R². Therefore E_A = E_B = E_C; the electric fields due to all three shells at 3R are equal in magnitude.

(b)(ii) C and A are the two ends of the semicircle. Both are at a distance of 5 cm (radius) from B and at a distance of √(5² + 10²) = √125 cm from D... Actually C and A are both on the semicircle, so they are both at 5 cm from B (the centre). The potential at any point on the semicircle due to both charges depends only on the distance from each charge. Since C and A are both at 5 cm from B and both at the same distance from D (since D is on the diameter and C, A are symmetric endpoints of the diameter), V_C = V_A. Therefore the work done in moving +5 μC from C to A is W = q(V_A - V_C) = 0.

questions.text_english:
(a)(i) A proton moving with velocity V⃗ in a non-uniform magnetic field traces a path as shown in the figure. The path followed by the proton is always in the plane of the paper. What is the direction of the magnetic field in the region near points P, Q and R? What can you say about relative magnitude of magnetic fields at these points?
(a)(ii) A current carrying circular loop of area A produces a magnetic field B at its centre. Show that the magnetic moment of the loop is 2BA/μ₀ × √(A/π).
OR
(b)(i) Derive an expression for the torque acting on a rectangular current loop suspended in a uniform magnetic field.
(b)(ii) A charged particle is moving in a circular path with velocity V⃗ in a uniform magnetic field B⃗. It is made to pass through a sheet of lead and as a consequence, it looses one half of its kinetic energy without change in its direction. How will (1) the radius of its path (2) its time period of revolution change?

key_points: (a)(i) Direction of B is into the page at P, Q, R (for proton curving as shown). At P the radius is smallest so B is largest; at R radius is largest so B is smallest; hence B_P > B_Q > B_R
(a)(ii) From B = μ₀I/2r and A = πr², r = √(A/π). Current I = 2Br/μ₀. Magnetic moment m = IA = 2Br/μ₀ × A = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π) × A = 2BA/μ₀ × √(A/π)
(b)(ii) KE becomes KE/2, so v' = v/√2. Radius r = mv/qB ∝ v, so new radius r' = r/√2. Time period T = 2πm/qB is independent of v, so T remains unchanged.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) The proton moves in the plane of the paper. The magnetic force provides centripetal acceleration. For the proton to curve as shown (curving upward/leftward), the magnetic force must point toward the centre of curvature. Using F⃗ = qv⃗ × B⃗ and the right-hand rule for a positive charge, the magnetic field must be directed into the page at all three points P, Q, and R. The radius of curvature r = mv/qB, so r ∝ 1/B (for constant m, v, q). At P the path is most curved (smallest radius), so B is largest at P. At R the path is least curved (largest radius), so B is smallest at R. Therefore: B_P > B_Q > B_R.

(a)(ii) For a circular loop of area A and radius r: A = πr², so r = √(A/π). The magnetic field at the centre is B = μ₀I/2r, giving I = 2Br/μ₀ = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π). The magnetic moment m = IA = (2B/μ₀)√(A/π) × A = 2BA/μ₀ × √(A/π). Hence proved.

(b)(i) Consider a rectangular loop of sides a and b carrying current I, suspended in a uniform magnetic field B. The forces on the two sides of length a (perpendicular to B) are F = BIa each, equal and opposite, forming a couple. The torque is τ = F × b sinθ = BIa × b sinθ = BIA sinθ, where θ is the angle between the plane of the loop and B (or τ = NIAB sinθ for N turns, and τ = m × B in vector form).

(b)(ii) When the particle passes through the lead sheet, KE reduces to KE/2. Since KE = (1/2)mv², the new speed v' = v/√2. The radius of circular motion r = mv/(qB) ∝ v, so new radius r' = mv'/(qB) = m(v/√2)/(qB) = r/√2. The radius decreases by a factor of √2. The time period T = 2πm/(qB), which depends only on m, q, and B (not on velocity). Therefore, the time period remains unchanged.

(a)(ii) I = 2Br/μ₀ और r = √(A/π) से m = IA = 2BA/μ₀ × √(A/π) सिद्ध होता है।

(2) Lights from two independent sources are not coherent. Explain.
(a)(ii) Two slits 0.1 mm apart are arranged 1.20 m from a screen. Light of wavelength 600 nm from a distant source is incident on the slits. (1) How far apart will adjacent bright interference fringes be on the screen? (2) Find the angular width (in degree) of the first bright fringe.

key_points: (a)(i) Coherent sources: sources with constant phase difference; necessary because the interference pattern is stable only if the phase relationship between the two sources does not change with time
Independent sources: atoms emit light independently with random phase; the phase difference changes randomly so no sustained pattern
(2) Angular width of first fringe = λ/d = 600×10⁻⁹/0.1×10⁻³ = 6×10⁻³ rad = 6×10⁻³ × (180/π) ≈ 0.344°

(b)(ii) First refraction at the first surface (air to glass): object at infinity, R = +15 cm, n₁=1, n₂=1.5; n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R → 1.5/v = 0.5/15 → v = 45 cm inside glass. Second refraction at far surface (glass to air): object at 45-30=15 cm to the right of second surface (so u = +15 cm going away), R = -15 cm, n₁=1.5, n₂=1; 1/v - 1.5/15 = (1-1.5)/(-15) → 1/v = 0.1 - 1/30... final image at 30 cm beyond the glass ball on the far side.

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(1) Coherent sources are sources of light that emit waves having a constant phase difference (which may be zero) between them and the same frequency. They are necessary for a sustained interference pattern because if the phase difference changes randomly with time, the positions of bright and dark fringes keep shifting, and the pattern averages out to uniform illumination, making it impossible to observe a stable interference pattern.
(2) Two independent sources such as two separate light bulbs or two separate portions of a source emit light through random, spontaneous atomic transitions. Each atom emits a wave train independently, and the phase of each emission is random. Therefore, the phase difference between waves from two independent sources changes randomly and rapidly (in about 10⁻⁸ s), making them incoherent. No sustained or stable interference pattern is possible.

(a)(ii)(1) Fringe width β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹ × 1.20)/(0.1×10⁻³) = 7.2×10⁻³ m = 7.2 mm. Adjacent bright fringes are 7.2 mm apart.
(2) Angular fringe width = λ/d = 600×10⁻⁹/0.1×10⁻³ = 6×10⁻³ rad. Converting to degrees: 6×10⁻³ × (180/π) ≈ 6×10⁻³ × 57.3 ≈ 0.344°.

(b)(i) A wavefront is the locus of all points in a medium that are vibrating in the same phase. When a plane wavefront falls on a convex lens, the central part of the wavefront passes through the thicker portion of the lens and is retarded more, while the edges pass through thinner portions. The emerging wavefront becomes spherical and converges at the focal point of the lens (for incident plane wave parallel to the axis).

(b)(ii) For refraction at the first surface (air→glass): n₁ = 1, n₂ = 1.5, R = +15 cm, u = ∞. Using n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R: 1.5/v - 0 = 0.5/15 = 1/30, so v = 45 cm from the first surface (inside glass). This image serves as the virtual object for the second surface. Distance from second surface: 45 - 30 = 15 cm (to the right of the second surface, so u = +15 cm). For second surface (glass→air): n₁ = 1.5, n₂ = 1, R = -15 cm (centre of curvature is to the left). n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R: 1/v - 1.5/15 = (1-1.5)/(-15) = 0.5/15 = 1/30. So 1/v = 1/30 + 1/10 = 1/30 + 3/30 = 4/30, giving v = 7.5 cm to the right of the second surface. The final image is formed 7.5 cm beyond the glass ball on the far side.
